tips.q: What photo works best for an AI action figure?
tips.a: Front-facing, full upper body, neutral background, sharp focus on the face. Group shots, side profiles, and sunglass selfies all hurt identity preservation. A casual phone selfie taken near a window in daylight beats a dim studio shot.

tips.q: How do I make the toy package text readable?
tips.a: Quote your exact strings (`name: "ALEX KIM"`, `tagline: "Limited Edition"`) and limit to 3 text fields per package. JSON-format prompts in this library handle layout and font sizing automatically — pick those when packaging text matters.

tips.q: Why doesn't my action figure look like me?
tips.a: Add `preserve facial features and hairstyle exactly` to the prompt, increase your reference photo resolution, or try a different sub-style — Funko Pop Style deliberately abstracts faces into chibi proportions and won't read as a 1:1 likeness.

tips.q: Can I make an action figure of two people?
tips.a: Yes — upload one image with both subjects clearly visible and use the Couple / Family Set sub-scene templates. GPT Image 2 keeps both faces accurate in a shared collector box without merging the identities.

faq.q: How do I turn my photo into an action figure with GPT Image 2?
faq.a: Upload a clear, full-body photo to GPT Image 2 Studio, paste the action figure prompt, customize your name, profession, and accessories — the model returns a 3D-toy-style image in blister packaging within 30 seconds.

faq.q: What's the best action figure prompt for ChatGPT?
faq.a: The most reliable template is: 'Create a 3D action figure of [name], displayed in clear plastic blister packaging like a collectible toy. Include accessories: [list]. Style: realistic 3D render, full-body, dramatic lighting.' Adjust accessories to match the person's profession or hobby.

faq.q: Can I use these prompts with the free version of GPT Image 2?
faq.a: Yes — GPT Image 2 Studio offers free trial credits (1K resolution = 6 credits per generation). Each action figure prompt typically requires 1 generation, so you can preview multiple variations before committing.

faq.q: Why does my action figure not look like me?
faq.a: Three common fixes: (1) upload a higher-resolution close-up of your face, (2) add 'preserve facial features and hairstyle exactly' to the prompt, (3) avoid heavy stylization keywords like 'cartoon' or 'anime' which override likeness.

faq.q: Can I make an action figure of two people (couple / friends)?
faq.a: Yes — upload a single image with both people clearly visible, then use a multi-figure prompt template like 'Create two action figures of the people in the photo in a shared collector box.' GPT Image 2's multi-image consistency keeps both faces accurate.
